claims.text: Real-time adaptive laser parameter control will improve the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components relative to fixed-parameter processing.
Real-time adaptive laser parameter control will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Real-time adaptive laser parameter control will reduce fabrication-induced defects.
Standard fixed laser parameters produce unstable melt-pool dynamics in high-entropy-alloy processing.
Unstable melt-pool dynamics lead to porosity, dimensional deviations, and nonuniform microstructures.
The proposed system uses in-situ melt-pool thermal imaging and machine learning to dynamically adjust laser power and scanning speed.
Laser power and scanning speed are process parameters that affect laser-processing quality.
Adaptive control stabilizes the melt pool by mitigating thermal fluctuations and excessive heat accumulation.
Melt-pool stabilization produces a more uniform microstructure with fewer porosity defects and lower residual stress.
Real-time feedback permits on-the-fly adjustment of laser energy input.
On-the-fly adjustment of laser energy input reduces thermal gradients and controls solidification rates.
Controlling thermal gradients and solidification rates minimizes porosity and phase segregation.
Reducing porosity and phase segregation enhances dimensional accuracy and mechanical performance.
Adaptive processing is predicted to produce parts with relative density greater than 98%.
Adaptive processing is predicted to improve dimensional tolerance relative to fixed-parameter processing.
Adaptive processing is predicted to increase strength and improve ductility.
The intervention is expected to apply to both laser powder bed fusion and directed energy deposition under routine controlled-atmosphere processing conditions.
Extreme variation in powder properties or environmental conditions may limit sensor integration and adaptive adjustment.
